notes: Step 1 parts kept unchanged; no parts added or dropped.
Circuit: board pin 2 -> green wire -> column 3 -> 220 ohm resistor (column 3 to column 6) -> LED anode (column 6); LED cathode (column 8) -> black wire -> board GND. This matches the schematic.

The image labels the breadboard half with rows f-j at the top. These holes are named with bank 'b' (rows f-j) to follow the catalogue's row-letter convention: resistor at 3b.h and 6b.h, LED at 6b.i and 8b.i, green wire at 3b.g, black wire at 8b.h.
The LED's anode is the bent, longer leg at column 6 and the cathode is the straight leg at column 8. This is the polarity the schematic requires.
The USB cable joins the board's USB port for power and programming. Its far end (the computer) is not modelled.
